title_ko: 이 컵이 하루 동안 지나간 곳
logline_en: One ordinary object is passed hand-to-hand through six places in one day; every hand-off is a whip-pan match cut, so the object never leaves the centre of frame.

evidence.claim: Third-party roundup reports transition-driven swap formats (spinning-fan outfit swap) trending on Reels in Oct 2026.

hypotheses: H1: Continuous-object match cuts keep viewers past the 3-second mark at a higher rate than our static-opening videos.
H2: Viewers rewatch to work out how each transition was done (avg view % > 90%).
why_now: PROVISIONAL: no platform-measured candidates could be collected in this session (YouTube key missing, Instagram/Apify hosts blocked); evidence below is secondary and unverified. Re-rank against measured clusters before production spend. Transfers the reported 'transition as payoff' mechanic to a non-fashion subject, where saturation is presumably lower (to be measured).
creative_principle: Make the edit itself the spectacle: one anchored subject, many worlds, each cut a small magic trick.
originality_notes: Only the abstract mechanic (match-cut swap) is borrowed; the subject, locations, people and music are our own.
format: live-action match-cut relay, no dialogue, captions as place labels
hooks_ko: 이 컵 하나로 서울 한 바퀴

storyboard.visual: Hand holds cup to camera at home
Back home; first hand receives it — loop

edit_plan: Shoot each hand-off as two halves of a whip pan at the same speed and direction; cut at peak motion blur.
audio_plan: Original or licensed 120 BPM track; cuts on downbeats.

assets_required.source: commissioned or royalty-free library with commercial social licence

success_metric: 3-second hold rate above account median; avg view % ≥ 90%.
risks: Transitions look cheap if whip speeds do not match
